monthly_review.summary: You've shifted toward higher-intensity running this month, with notable gains in pace and cadence but reduced aerobic volume and efficiency. HR has risen meaningfully, indicating increased physiological demand.
monthly_review.highlight: Your Zone 4 time jumped from 3% to 21% of total HR zone distribution — a dramatic shift toward threshold work, likely driving the 19-sec/km pace improvement but at the cost of aerobic base volume.

goal_tracker.message: You need 22.3 more km across 5 remaining sessions — averaging 4.5 km per run — to match last month’s distance. Given your recent 11.1 km long run, you can achieve this with one more long run (~10 km) and four moderate runs (~3–4 km each).

insights.title: Declining efficiency despite faster pace
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency dropped from 13.42 to 13.19 m/sec per bpm while avg pace improved — suggesting less economical movement at higher intensities, possibly due to elevated vertical oscillation (9.2 cm on 7:03/km effort) and inconsistent stride length (range: 68.8–94.7 cm across same-day runs).

insights.title: Zone 4 dominance replacing Zone 2 foundation
insights.body: Zone 4 contribution rose from 3% (May) to 21% (June), while Zone 2 fell from 43% to 32% — a 11-point reallocation away from foundational aerobic development toward threshold stress.

insights.title: Cadence-stride trade-off under fatigue
insights.body: Cadence increased +4 spm overall, yet stride length varied widely (69.7–94.7 cm) — notably, your fastest effort (7:03/km, 159 bpm) had longest stride (94.7 cm) and highest vertical oscillation (9.2 cm), suggesting form compromise at intensity.

insights.title: High-intensity clustering without recovery buffer
insights.body: Three runs on June 4 — including a hard 1.0 km at 159 bpm (Z4) — occurred within 4 hours; ground contact time remained stable (~311–330 ms), but aerobic TE (0.7–2.6) and HR variability were not captured, raising recovery uncertainty.

recommendations.action: Replace one upcoming run with a 45-min Zone 2 session (HR ≤135 bpm, pace ~9:30–10:00/km) focused solely on relaxed breathing and cadence consistency (target 148–152 spm).
recommendations.reason: Zone 2 volume dropped 11% MoM and is critical for rebuilding aerobic efficiency and HR resilience — your current Z2 % (32%) is below the 40–50% ideal for sustainable base development.

recommendations.action: Perform a 10-min post-run stride drill session after your next easy run: 2x2 min barefoot or minimalist strides at 152 spm, focusing on light ground contact (<300 ms) and minimizing vertical oscillation (<7.5 cm).
recommendations.reason: Your vertical oscillation spiked to 9.2 cm during high-cadence/high-HR efforts, and ground contact remains >310 ms — both limit efficiency gains despite cadence improvement.

recommendations.action: Delay your next long run by 2 days if your avg HR over the prior 3 runs exceeds 142 bpm or if any run shows aerobic TE < 2.0.
recommendations.reason: Your June 7 long run (11.1 km, HR 141, TE 3.4) was well-executed, but repeated high-HR efforts (e.g., June 1: HR 147, TE 3.5; June 4: HR 159, TE 2.6) suggest accumulating fatigue — protecting recovery preserves long-run quality.

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish neuromuscular coordination and cardiovascular efficiency at low intensity to restore economy, lower HR drift, and rebalance zone distribution — prioritizing sustainability over speed.
suggested_sessions: 30-min conversational-paced run with cadence focus (148–152 spm)
